subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit parent-self-only tool denial policy for delegated sessions, and if so should the public syntax be `selfDeny`, `delegateOnly`, or part of a broader spawned-session permission model?
rationale: This changes the command/file-tool authorization boundary between parent and child sessions, so automation cannot choose the permanent config/API contract or security semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design delegate-only policy
options.body: Adopt an explicit delegate-only/self-deny policy with deny-wins semantics, audit visibility, docs, and native/ACP/gateway coverage before implementation.

options.title: Keep monotonic inheritance
options.body: Keep the current rule that child sessions cannot regain tools removed from the requester, accepting separate agent profiles or prompt guidance as the supported pattern.

options.title: Fold into broader permissions work
options.body: Defer this issue into the per-spawn/per-binding permissions model so one public API handles both child narrowing and parent-self-only delegation.

recommendation.title: Design delegate-only policy
recommendation.body: Adopt an explicit delegate-only/self-deny policy with deny-wins semantics, audit visibility, docs, and native/ACP/gateway coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest product/security decision owner signal from related issue reviews and repository maintainer routing evidence.
